events.title: Martin Fowler publishes Refactoring
events.summary: Martin Fowler published Refactoring in 1999 — cataloging code improvement patterns that complement his contemporaneous quote defining refactoring as behavior-preserving structure change.
events.about: Fowler's catalog gave names to extract-method, move-field, and dozens of safe transformations IDEs now automate. He shaped agile, microservices, and enterprise patterns discourse for Java and beyond.

narrative.whyChosen: Refactoring vocabulary became standard in IDEs and code review culture.
narrative.whyImportant: It legitimized changing structure without changing behavior as professional practice.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams feared improving messy code without a shared pattern language.

events.title: Extreme Programming Explained
events.summary: Kent Beck published Extreme Programming Explained in 1999 — popularizing pair programming, TDD, and iterative delivery.
events.about: XP influenced Agile Manifesto authors and every modern CI/CD pipeline. Beck also created JUnit — the ancestor of xUnit frameworks in every language.

narrative.whyChosen: Beck connected testing, pairing, and iteration into a named methodology.
narrative.whyImportant: TDD and continuous integration became industry defaults.
narrative.problemSolved: Waterfall planning failed for fast-changing software products.

events.title: Martin Fowler defines refactoring
events.quoteText: Refactoring is a controlled technique for incrementally improving the design of an existing code base.
events.summary: Martin Fowler's book Refactoring gives refactoring a precise definition and a catalog of safe code transformations.
events.about: Before Fowler, 'refactoring' was vague cleanup work. His catalog — extract method, move field, rename — became IDE menu items and code review vocabulary. The definition still anchors agile discussions of paying down debt without changing behavior.

narrative.whyChosen: The sentence that turned refactoring from slang into engineering practice.
narrative.whyImportant: It legitimized structural code changes as a disciplined, test-backed activity.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams feared changing working code without a shared pattern language.
